aspects.says: A hand-written compareAndSet loop reads, decides and swaps, and after a failed swap decides again on the new value; a decision kept from the first attempt is a check-then-act.
basis: section:An Atomic Update Retries Until Its compareAndSet Wins, So Its Function Can Run Many Times

aspects.says: ConcurrentHashMap.compute and merge are atomic for one call on one key; an action made of two calls can be seen half done, so values that must agree go under one key.
basis: section:compute and merge Are Atomic for One Key, Not for an Action Across Keys

aspects.says: ConcurrentHashMap.compute runs its function exactly once per call, while other updates to the same bin wait.
basis: section:compute and merge Are Atomic for One Key, Not for an Action Across Keys
aspects.reason: a count of function runs under contention differs from run to run and isn't a deterministic grade; the bin-transfer practice relies on it without grading it

aspects.says: A rule over two variables breaks even when each is atomic; it holds only under one lock or in one immutable holder replaced by compareAndSet with the rule checked on every attempt.
basis: section:Values That Must Agree Need One Lock or One Immutable Holder Replaced by compareAndSet

aspects.says: LongAdder spreads contending updates over cells and is faster than AtomicLong under contention, but sum() is not an atomic snapshot and it has no compareAndSet to make decisions with.
basis: section:LongAdder Counts Faster Under Contention Because No Single Variable Holds the Total

aspects.says: An atomic class's updateAndGet, getAndUpdate or accumulateAndGet is a compare-and-set retried until it wins, so the function passed to it can run several times per call; a side effect belongs after the update, decided from the value it returned.
basis: section:An Atomic Update Retries Until Its compareAndSet Wins, So Its Function Can Run Many Times
